# sysutils_package (Data Source)

Reads whether an OS package is installed, its version and architecture, and the version the local package index offers, with the same package manager backends as `sysutils_package`: `apt` on Debian and Ubuntu, `dnf` or `yum` on Fedora and RHEL-like distributions, `apk` on Alpine. Only read-only queries run (`dpkg-query` and `apt-cache policy`, `rpm -q` and `repoquery -C`, `apk info`, `apk list` and `apk policy`), so nothing on the host changes and no root privileges are needed, unless `refresh_cache` is set.

The data source uses the same package manager backends and the same detection as the [`sysutils_package`](../resources/package.md) resource, so `version` has the form that the resource's `version` accepts. A package that is not installed, or that no repository has, is not an error: `installed` is false and the version attributes are null.

## What is run

| Package manager | Installed version and architecture | `available_version` |
|-----------------|------------------------------------|---------------------|
| `apt` | `dpkg-query --show` | The candidate of `apt-cache policy`, which honours pinning |
| `dnf`, `yum` | `rpm --query` | The newest version of `repoquery -C --available --latest-limit=1`, for the installed architecture, else `noarch` or the host's |
| `apk` | `apk info --installed` and `apk list --installed` | The newest version that `apk policy` lists in a repository without a tag |

None of these commands changes the host or needs root. They read the package index as it is: `dnf` and `yum` run in cache-only mode (`-C`), so that they don't download metadata that has expired, as they otherwise would. With `refresh_cache = true`, the index is refreshed first, which does change the host (see below).

## Example Usage

### Read a package

```terraform
data "sysutils_package" "nginx" {
  name = "nginx"
}

output "nginx" {
  value = {
    installed    = data.sysutils_package.nginx.installed
    version      = data.sysutils_package.nginx.version      # null if not installed
    architecture = data.sysutils_package.nginx.architecture # "amd64", "x86_64", "noarch", ...
    available    = data.sysutils_package.nginx.available_version
    manager      = data.sysutils_package.nginx.package_manager # "apt", "dnf", "yum" or "apk"
  }
}
```

### Configure software only where it is installed

```terraform
data "sysutils_package" "docker" {
  name = "docker-ce"
}

# Configure the Docker daemon only on hosts that have Docker installed,
# without installing it anywhere.
resource "sysutils_file" "docker_daemon" {
  count = data.sysutils_package.docker.installed ? 1 : 0

  path    = "/etc/docker/daemon.json"
  content = jsonencode({ "log-driver" = "journald" })
}
```

### Check for an available update

```terraform
# Refresh the package index while planning, then report whether the index
# offers another version of openssl than the installed one. Needs root.
data "sysutils_package" "openssl" {
  name          = "openssl"
  refresh_cache = true
}

output "openssl_update_available" {
  value = (
    data.sysutils_package.openssl.installed &&
    data.sysutils_package.openssl.available_version != null &&
    data.sysutils_package.openssl.available_version != data.sysutils_package.openssl.version
  )
}
```

`refresh_cache` runs `apt-get update`, `dnf makecache`, `yum makecache` or `apk update` whenever the data source is read, which includes every `terraform plan`. It needs root and network access to the repositories. The refresh waits for the provider's package-manager lock, which `sysutils_package` also takes, and runs at most once per provider run, even if several data sources and `sysutils_package` resources with `update_cache` ask for it.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the package, such as `"nginx"`. The same names as in `sysutils_package` are accepted: 1 to 128 letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `+` or `-`, starting with a letter or digit; with apt, lowercase and at least 2 characters. Architecture qualifiers, version constraints, globs, file paths and virtual `provides` are not accepted.

### Optional

- `manager` (String) Package manager to query: `"apt"`, `"dnf"`, `"yum"` or `"apk"`. `"auto"` or unset uses the first of them whose tools are installed, in that order, as `sysutils_package` does. Reading fails if the manager is not installed.
- `refresh_cache` (Boolean) Refresh the package index (`apt-get update`, `dnf makecache`, `yum makecache`, `apk update`) before reading `available_version`. This changes the host, needs root privileges and network access to the repositories, and happens whenever the data source is read, including during `terraform plan`. The refresh waits for, and holds, the provider's package-manager lock, which `sysutils_package` also takes, and happens at most once per provider run, shared with `update_cache` of `sysutils_package`. Defaults to `false`.

### Read-Only

- `architecture` (String) Architecture of the installed package, in the package manager's terms: such as `"amd64"` or `"all"` with apt, `"x86_64"` or `"noarch"` with dnf and yum, `"x86_64"` or `"noarch"` with apk. With several architectures installed, that of the first one the package database lists. Null if the package is not installed.
- `available_version` (String) Version that installing or upgrading the package would select from the local package index: apt's candidate as `apt-cache policy` shows it, which honours pinning and may be the installed version; with dnf and yum the newest version in the enabled repositories, from the downloaded metadata (`repoquery -C`); with apk the newest version in a repository without a tag. Null if the package is in no repository, or if the index has not been downloaded, as in fresh container images; set `refresh_cache` to download it.
- `id` (String) Data source identifier (equal to `name`).
- `installed` (Boolean) Whether the package is installed, according to the package database. With apt, packages that are only half-installed or whose configuration files remain after removal are not installed.
- `package_manager` (String) Package manager that was queried: `"apt"`, `"dnf"`, `"yum"` or `"apk"`.
- `version` (String) Installed version, in the form the package database reports and `version` of `sysutils_package` accepts: `[epoch:]upstream[-revision]` for apt, `[epoch:]version-release` for dnf and yum, `version-rN` for apk. Null if the package is not installed.

## Errors

| Situation | Diagnostic |
|-----------|------------|
| `manager` names a package manager that is not installed, or `manager` is unset and none is | `Package manager not available` |
| `name` breaks the rules of the package manager, such as an uppercase name with apt | `Invalid package name` |
| A query fails, for example because the package database is corrupt | `Querying package` |
| `refresh_cache = true` and the refresh fails, for example without root | `Updating package index` |
| The provider's `root_dir` is set | `Not supported with root_dir` |

## Caveats

- `available_version` is null where the package index has not been downloaded, as in fresh container images and after `dnf clean all`. Run the provider as root with dnf and yum: run as another user, they may look for metadata in a cache directory of that user's, and find none.
- With apt, `available_version` is apt's candidate: it can equal `version` although a repository has a newer version, if pinning holds that back. With dnf, yum and apk it is the newest version in the repositories, even if an installed package built elsewhere is newer. Compare the two with `!=` rather than ordering them: the package managers' version formats don't sort as strings.
- The data source reads the running host, so it refuses to work when the provider's `root_dir` is set. Use a provider configuration without `root_dir` for it.
- It is read during planning. A package that a `sysutils_package` resource in the same configuration installs is only seen if the data source depends on the resource, for example by setting `name = sysutils_package.app.name`.
